finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated into the query string. An attacker can inject SQLite expressions, for example a CASE/subquery boolean blind or error-based extraction of data from any table the connection can read, such as `sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)`. Stacked queries are not available via PDO query on SQLite in most configurations, but data exfiltration is possible.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' takes raw user input with no validation
$sort is concatenated directly into the SQL string and executed with PDO::query()

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting or escaping in list_users_sorted. No authentication or authorization check anywhere in the file. Prepared statements cannot parameterize ORDER BY identifiers, and none are used here. By contrast, list_users_safe (line 10-12) uses an allowlist map, and find_user (line 16-17) uses a bound parameter, so both are not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: none in list_users_sorted; the allowlist at list.php:10-11 and the bound parameter at list.php:16-17 belong to other functions
verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 pass raw $_GET['sort'] into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query() string with no allowlist, cast or auth check, so an anonymous attacker can inject SQLite expressions. Caveat: no caller of list_users_sorted exists in this directory, so reachability depends on code outside it.
